subtitle.en: Four big birds of the shore and open water

intro.en:
For the last lesson of part 2, we stay on the coast, with four big birds. They are easy to recognise when you know what to look for, and some are a surprisingly new sight in Britain: the Little Egret was a rarity until the 1990s.

Big birds are good news for beginners: you can see them from far away, and their shape tells you a lot. A gull-like bird that dives from the sky, a snow-white heron with golden feet, a black bird with its wings hung out to dry, and a smart black-and-white duck.

At the end there's a quiz of eight questions, with birds from the last two lessons mixed in.

explain.en: The long flight feathers at the tip of the wing.
A patch on the thigh, just above the leg.
A long, wispy feather, on the head, neck or back.

look_for.en: Black bill and black legs, with yellow feet
In spring: long **plumes** on the head and back

where_when.en: Estuaries, marshes, rivers and lakes, mostly in the south and east. Runs through the shallows, stirring up fish with its feet.

describe.en: A harsh, croaking "arrk", given in flight or at a roost.

sound.status: chosen on xeno-canto details; listen before use

note.en: The first Little Egrets bred in Britain in 1996. Now there are thousands.

dont_confuse.en: Grey Heron (week 2): bigger and grey, with a pale yellow bill.

look_for.en: Black, with a white **thigh patch** in spring
White cheek, yellow at the gape
Perches with its wings spread out to dry

where_when.en: Coasts, estuaries, rivers and lakes, inland too. Dives for fish and then sits on a post, with its wings held out.

describe.en: A deep, croaking "gorrk", usually only heard at colonies.

sound.status: chosen on xeno-canto details; listen before use

look_for.en: Big, black-and-white duck, with a dark green head
Broad chestnut band round the breast
Bright red bill (a knob in the male, in spring)

where_when.en: Muddy estuaries and shores, and the occasional gravel pit. Sweeps its bill through the mud, and nests in rabbit burrows.

describe.en: A deep, nasal "ah-ah-ah" and, in spring, a whistled "wheee".

sound.status: chosen on xeno-canto details; listen before use

note.en: It is closer to a goose than to a duck, and much bigger than a Mallard.

look_for.en: Big and white, with a long pointed bill
Black **primaries** at the tip of the wings
Dives into the sea from a great height, with folded wings

where_when.en: Over the sea, and at big cliff colonies like Bass Rock, Grassholm and Bempton. Around half the world's Gannets nest in Britain and Ireland.

describe.en: A harsh, rhythmic "arrah-arrah", from a colony, with thousands going at once.

sound.status: chosen on xeno-canto details; listen before use

note.en: Young birds are dark brown with white spots, and slowly turn white over five years.

outside.en: Go to the coast this week. Scan the sea for a white bird, diving with its wings folded. Look at the rocks, the posts and the groynes for a Cormorant with its wings spread. In the south or east, check the estuary for a snow-white egret.
